passage:
Subject: About Sunday

Dear Mridul,

I keep thinking about Sunday on the hostel roof. You told me the placement interview didn't go through, and I could feel the sentence "there will be other chances" sitting in my mouth, ready to go. I swallowed it. Instead I said, "You sound really disappointed." You went quiet, then said, "I practised for weeks." And after that everything came out, the questions you had blanked on, the part that stung most. I only nodded and stayed. Thank you for trusting me with it. Next time you want ideas, just say so, and I'll gladly help.

Vikas

qa.q: Where were Vikas and Mridul on Sunday?
qa.a: On the hostel roof.

qa.q: What was Vikas feeling when the sentence "there will be other chances" was sitting in the mouth?
qa.a: An urge to reassure and fix things quickly. Vikas felt that, and chose to swallow it and reflect Mridul's feeling instead.

qa.q: What did Vikas do that let Mridul go deeper?
qa.a: Vikas named the emotion by saying "You sound really disappointed," then stayed and nodded instead of offering quick comfort.

qa.q: How might Mridul feel after hearing "You sound really disappointed"?
qa.a: Understood, and safe enough to say more. Mridul answered "I practised for weeks" and then shared the questions that had been blanked on.

grounding: A young adult reflects Mridul's emotion back instead of reassuring, and Mridul goes deeper.

passage:
Host: So what did you do when Binita came back from her viva?

Yogesh: Honestly, my first thought was to say "Don't worry, you always do well." I'm Yogesh, by the way. But she was standing in the doorway with her bag still on, not saying anything, so I just said, "You sound really let down." She sort of laughed, and then she sat on my bed and said, "They asked about the one chapter I skipped revising." After that it went on for a long time. She talked about the examiner's face, and what she wished she'd said. I mostly said "mm" and "that must have felt awful." Later she said, "Thanks for not fixing it." That stuck with me.

qa.q: What did Binita say about the viva after sitting down?
qa.a: "They asked about the one chapter I skipped revising."

qa.q: What was Yogesh's first thought when Binita came back, and what did Yogesh do instead?
qa.a: Yogesh first thought of saying "Don't worry, you always do well," but instead named the feeling: "You sound really let down."

qa.q: What small step helped Binita talk more?
qa.a: Yogesh reflected the feeling in a few words and then mostly listened with sounds like "mm" and "that must have felt awful," rather than fixing anything.

qa.q: Why might Binita have said "Thanks for not fixing it"?
qa.a: Binita may have wanted to be understood first. Advice or quick reassurance could have felt like a way to move past the feeling.

grounding: A young adult tells the story of reflecting Binita's disappointment in words, and Binita talks more.

passage: I share a hostel room with Shalini, so I heard the whole thing from my bed. Sudha came in, dropped her bag and said the internship list was out and her name wasn't on it. She started explaining: the interview had gone well, the manager had smiled, she had prepared for weeks. Shalini didn't give advice. She waited until Sudha paused and said, "You sound really disappointed. Like you'd let yourself hope." Sudha went quiet. Then she said, in a different voice, "I told my father I'd get it. He's been telling everyone." I don't know what was going on inside her, but that was the part she hadn't said before. They talked for an hour after that, mostly about her father. Shalini hardly spoke. When Sudha left, she hugged Shalini for a long time.

qa.q: Whose name wasn't on the internship list?
qa.a: Sudha's name wasn't on it.

qa.q: What was Sudha feeling underneath her first explanation?
qa.a: Sudha was disappointed and also worried about letting her father down, which came out only after Shalini named the feeling.

qa.q: Why did Shalini's words help Sudha go deeper?
qa.a: Shalini reflected the emotion instead of giving advice, which showed she was listening for feelings and let Sudha share the harder part about her father.

qa.q: How might Sudha's father be part of what she was carrying?
qa.a: He had been telling everyone she would get it, so she probably felt pressure and dreaded disappointing him.

grounding: Shows a young adult reflecting a friend's emotion, which lets the friend go deeper, as seen by a roommate.

passage:
Monday: Sangeeta told Chaitanya about her sister's wedding preparations. "Everyone's asking about the caterer, the lights, the guests." Chaitanya jumped in: "Just make a spreadsheet, divide the jobs." Sangeeta nodded and changed the subject.
Thursday: She mentioned it again over tea. This time Chaitanya stopped himself. "It sounds like you're doing everything and nobody's noticing you." Sangeeta put her cup down. "Yes. Exactly. Nobody's asked how I am once." She talked for twenty minutes about feeling invisible in her own family.
Two weeks later: Sangeeta messaged him first. "Can I tell you about today? You're good at getting it." Chaitanya smiled at the screen and called her.

qa.q: What did Chaitanya suggest on Monday?
qa.a: Just make a spreadsheet and divide the jobs.

qa.q: What was Sangeeta feeling underneath the talk of wedding jobs?
qa.a: She felt invisible and unappreciated in her own family, since nobody had asked how she was.

qa.q: What changed between Monday and Thursday in how Chaitanya listened?
qa.a: On Thursday he reflected her feeling instead of offering a fix, which let Sangeeta open up about feeling invisible.

qa.q: What might Chaitanya feel when Sangeeta messaged him first?
qa.a: He probably felt pleased and trusted, smiling at the screen before calling her.

grounding: Shows a young adult learning to reflect a friend's feeling instead of giving advice, which lets her share more deeply.

passage:
"Amandeep, you asked how to help your friend who's going through the breakup," said Pallavi aunty, setting down the teacups. "Let me tell you about Kusum. We were twenty, sharing a room in the working women's hostel in Pune. One night she came back and told me, very flatly, that her fiancé had called off the wedding. Then she started talking about the caterer, the invitations, what to tell relatives.
I wanted to fix things. I almost said, 'You'll find someone better.' But I stopped. I said, 'You sound so hurt. And maybe a bit ashamed?' She looked at me, and her face just broke. We sat up till two. She told me things she hadn't told her own mother.
So, beta. Don't rush to fix. Listen for the feeling underneath, and say it back."

qa.q: Where were Pallavi aunty and Kusum living at twenty?
qa.a: In the working women's hostel in Pune.

qa.q: What was Kusum feeling underneath her talk about the caterer and invitations?
qa.a: She was deeply hurt and perhaps ashamed, which came out when Pallavi named those feelings.

qa.q: What was the turning point in the story?
qa.a: Pallavi stopping herself from saying 'You'll find someone better' and instead reflecting Kusum's hurt, which let Kusum open up.

qa.q: How might Kusum have felt when Pallavi named her feelings?
qa.a: She probably felt seen and less alone, which is why her face broke and she talked until two.

grounding: Shows an elder recalling how reflecting a friend's emotion instead of fixing let the friend go deeper.

passage: Platform 4 at Dadar was packed, and every thirty seconds an announcement boomed overhead. Pradeep had been talking since they got off the bus. "So the coach just read out the list, and my name wasn't on it. After three years of trials. Whatever. It's just the state team." Deepika leaned in close to hear over a train horn. She didn't say, "Next year for sure." She said, "Three years of trials. You sound gutted, not whatever." Pradeep looked at her, then at the tracks. The next announcement drowned everything out, so she waited it through. "Yeah," he said at last. "Gutted. And kind of embarrassed, because I told the whole family I'd make it this time." They let the 6:12 go by. He kept talking, and this time it was the real story.

qa.q: Which train did they let go by?
qa.a: They let the 6:12 go by.

qa.q: What was Deepika thinking when she chose not to say "Next year for sure"?
qa.a: She sensed that Pradeep's "whatever" was hiding hurt, and cared more about hearing him than cheering him up.

qa.q: Why did Deepika's reply work better than a quick reassurance?
qa.a: Naming the feeling behind "whatever" invited Pradeep to go deeper instead of being cheered past it.

qa.q: How did Deepika's words affect Pradeep?
qa.a: He felt understood enough to admit he was gutted and embarrassed, and began telling the real story.

grounding: Shows a young adult reflecting the feeling behind a friend's casual words on a noisy platform, which lets him open up.
